Top candidates: **Gray Mold** (gray-brown velvety spore mass), **Rhizopus Soft Rots** (whitish-gray mycelia with black sporangia), **Sclerotinia** (white cottony mycelium).

Let me check reference images for my top candidates, one at a time.

The Rhizopus seed image (5369124) is nearly identical to the test image (5369123) - both show the same dense whitish-gray mycelial web with dark black sporangia scattered throughout, same close-up macro view. These are from the same Bugwood image series (5369119, 5369121, 5369123, 5369124 all Rhizopus).

**Summary of comparisons:**
- **Rhizopus_Soft_Rots** (stem/5369121, seed/5369124): Extremely strong match - same gray mycelial network, same dark sporangia dots, same macro close-up style
- Gray_Mold: Brown stem lesions or V-shaped leaf lesions, no matching mycelial web
- Sclerotinia: White mycelium with distinct sclerotia, different texture
- Southern_Blight: Stem cross-section necrosis, no mycelial web
- Late_Blight/Alternaria: Microscopic spore images, completely different
- Early_Blight: Leaf spots with concentric rings, different

The test image shows the characteristic Rhizopus mycelial network with black sporangia (sporangiophores with sporangia) in macro close-up view.
